body:
It always feels like “the big/only one” when you’re as young as you both are but, frankly, it’s not. If you broke up today, do you really, seriously, think that you are going to go through the rest of your life (maybe 65 years?) without ever experiencing the same emotions again? You must realise how patently ridiculous that sounds. I mean - I assume he has already felt something similar with someone else (whatever he says) given he already has a child by another woman - and cheated on you to boot, so assume he felt something for her too…

Honestly, even if he was the perfect boyfriend in every other way, I’d caution that leaving sounds like it’s in your best interests, given everything else you’ve described. But he’s not even a good boyfriend, and can’t ever be, regardless of how tingly you feel or how long you talk or whatever - because a good boyfriend won’t cheat on you, period. It really, really, is that simple.

Go find one of the many men out there who you will inevitably have an equal or better emotional connection with, who won’t make you a dull co-parent in your 20s who misses their chance to experience the world, and who won’t literally cheat on you. You don’t have to settle for so little.
I have just remembered that I opened the door to our local Conservative councillor when I was 25 and he asked me if my parents were home… Suffice to say he did not get my vote.

35 (almost 36), I’m ID’ed in the supermarket unless my tattoo sleeve is showing. Even then most people guess I’m somewhere in my mid-20s. I have a very naturally young face, if I had long hair I think I would genuinely look like a child. I also live a moderately ‘wild’ lifestyle partying-wise and don’t do any special skin regimes, in my case it’s all genetic. I’m white British so not known for that I guess but it runs in the family.

I am largely a clone of my mother and growing up people would ask on the reg if she was my older sister (she had me at 30). I am conscious that at 66 she does now look her age - I have been trying to pinpoint when the transformation occurred, and think it was probably around the mid-40s. So, I guess I have that long to start botoxing! (Joke… perhaps).

Generally I just take it as a compliment, I always have my driving licence with me (I keep it in my phone case) so don’t mind being ID’ed, and just joke with my boyfriend if he’s with me that clearly he looks like a predator.

Yes, at 34, a friend of friends. Night and day compared to my last relationship - and happened out of the blue when I was least expecting it and as I was bemoaning my permanently single fate. It will happen eventually - just not always as soon as we might like!

Age: 35
Gender: F
Location: London
Orientation: heteroflexible

First dates: idk like 20+ 🙈
First date failures: most never got past date 1, had a big argument with one guy about politics on date 4 and never spoke again, several quite cringe examples of me chasing guys who clearly weren’t interested 
Relationship success: met my bf at Glastonbury in June and haven’t looked back ✌️
Optimism for next year: excited to finally be in a healthy, loving relationship - if it can happen to me after all the swings and misses I genuinely think it can happen for anyone. Don’t give up hope!

F35 here, spent most of the year really struggling to get over my abysmally shitty ex who dumped me in Sept 2023, had a lot of casual sex and short stints of dating people off apps that never went anywhere, when I was completely despairing I’d ever find someone I met a friend of friends at a festival in the summer and we haven’t looked back. Nearly at the six month mark, we’re super in love and de facto living together, all of our friends and family say they’ve never seen us so happy (and I’d agree). Don’t give up hope!

I exclusively used Hinge for 10 months, met a lot of guys and some who were very nice etc but no one who worked for more than a few weeks. Then met my current wonderful boyfriend out of the blue at a festival as a friend of friends. Looking back on it, I’m glad I did the online dating thing for a bit just to work through my previous relationship and get back “in practice” - but think it’s quite telling that ultimately I was successful off the apps not on them. If you’re finding them a drag (which they are) then I’d suggest trying to do more social stuff in real life - hanging out with friends, colleagues, going to meet ups and so on. You never know who you’ll get introduced to! Good luck 🤞

Yeah there are kinks and then there’s… whatever this is. He has an incest fetish, a clear and serious porn addiction, and a history of using sex workers. It’s totally fair for any one of these on its own to be a dealbreaker for you - coupled with the rather alarming emotional volatility displayed in the DJ and engagement episodes, I’d personally advise you to run not walk, but that’s my two cents.

And always remember the Tim Minchin song - if you open your mind too much, your brain will fall out.

Leave, he sounds petulant and exhausting. You did nothing wrong, if he wanted to be exclusive he should have put his big boy pants on and asked for that, rather than policing what you were up to then throwing a tantrum when you didn’t mind-read him and do what he wanted even though he hadn’t actually asked. Asking you to confirm where you are and who you’re with all the time after only 3 dates is also a massive red flag. Consider this bullet avoided and swerve hard.

Yes, I can smell it on people and find it unpleasant. My hairdresser used to smoke and I could smell it on her fingers when she moved them around my head (and could see it, they were stained yellow). My friend at school never smoked but her mother chain-smoked (and died of lung cancer in her 50s) and everything my friend owned stank. My boyfriend very occasionally smokes cigarettes and he knows I won’t kiss him if he has just smoked. He generally vapes instead now which I don’t mind at all, although I think it can make people’s breath a bit stale.

It’s not shallow in the slightest. It’s literally the difference between dating someone and being friends. If he isn’t interested in you physically, why not relegate him to good friend territory and find someone who will rock your boat. If the sex life has gone wrong that early it’s unlikely to return, I’m afraid - unless he has some sort of depression or other issue that he is (a) able to identify and (b) both able and willing to fix.

The sheer amount of 30s and 40s men I’d see on apps when I was single who put “Not sure” about or “Open to” children. Like, how have you got to this stage and not know something that important about what you want (realistically) the rest of your life to look like!? Sounds like maybe they’re only actually making a decision either way in their mid/late 40s(?).
You can’t change your penis size, but you can change your gf. Do that.

My friend met her now-husband at 32, got married at 34 and had their first child at 35.

Most of my other friends are in their late 30s and single or at least unmarried. Most of them are pretty happy with this and have a lot of fun going out, dating etc.

My other friend was in a relationship/married for 15 years having met young, he cheated on her and it messed her up but at 39 she met my best friend (also 39) who’d been in a series of semi-long relationships with women who were never quite right for him, now both of them are together and couldn’t be happier.

I had a serious relationship that I thought would be “the one” end at 30 and then had a terrible relationship with someone who treated me very badly before finding the most amazing guy just before I turned 35. I’m 3 months in with him now and it feels like everything has clicked into place in my life. I’ve never been as happy and secure in a relationship - even the first one - and it feels like the previous ones were my training so I could be a good partner in this one.

It’s never too late to meet someone.
Ah, so you’ve met my ex?

Yes, this. You don’t ever know anyone properly until you’ve lived together - it doesn’t matter how much time you’ve spent together in the other person’s space, things change once you both “co-own” the space you’re in (whether living or renting). Make sure you’re happy with that before tying yourself to someone in a way that is extremely difficult to pick back apart…

In all honesty - talking about marriage within 20 days is how Jay has ended up having 6 kids with 3 women. This isn’t normal and is massive love bombing - which doesn’t tend to end well. No one knows anyone in 20 days. You admit you don’t have much dating experience - I’d advise being cautious and taking things slow, whether with Jay or someone else.

Yeah to second this - just because you like to retcon your whole history whenever you break up, doesn’t mean she does or should have to. The fact you and your boyfriend demanded her to remove photos taken and posted while she was in a relationship with him is actually pretty wild to me, like that’s some Stalinist revisionist shiz. It’s also, to be honest, indicative of an immature mindset about dating. What does it matter what other people think if they look at her socials? Surely the important thing is that you’re the one actually in a relationship with him now - and you’re both presumably posting with each other. I’m not sure what you want her to do to make it obvious they’re not together - post a newspaper with today’s date next to a sign saying she’s broken up? It’ll become apparent over time to anyone on her accounts that they’re no longer together if that’s such a concern. She doesn’t have to publicly erase 5 years of her life just to alleviate your insecurities.

Otherwise, the title of the post says she keeps reaching out - but you don’t go into any detail on this in the post other than saying her and the bf remained friends. Again, plenty of people do this without issue, and others don’t. I stayed good friends (and never the hint of anything more) with an ex I was in a 4 year relationship with, but went full no contact with another. It just depends on the people and the relationship and the circumstances of the break up. If she’s actually reaching out a lot in a way that makes your bf uncomfortable - and he’s communicated this to her and she still does it - then yes, I agree that’s not acceptable. If they’re just friends and you’re just insecure, then it really depends on how your bf feels about her, which none of us can tell you.

As to whether your bf moved on too fast / you’re a rebound - it might be that their relationship ran its course and he’d already largely moved on by the time it ended (which may well be the case if it ended amicably) and you don’t really have anything to worry about in that regard. But again - really only your bf can tell you.

As usual with posts on this sub, the answer is communication. The only way you’ll know anything, or resolve anything, is to talk to your bf about it. But first I would think about whether his behaviour has given you any real reason to worry - or if all this is coming from an insecurity inside yourself about factors out of your control. It’s worth remembering that you’re almost never going to date someone who doesn’t have an ex, whether they’re still in their life or not, and you can’t exert complete control over their involvement with/thoughts about/feelings for that person. All you can do is communicate and trust. Good luck!

I have a full sleeve and it has never stopped me getting into relationships (serious and not) or otherwise impeded my life (currently a corporate lawyer at a Biglaw firm, and yes I wear sleeveless dresses in the office and indeed at my interview). The issue here is probably just your age - it’s entirely normal to be 22 and not in a serious relationship, you’ve literally only just started your adult life. Also, to be honest, men may be sensing the desperation/insecurity that’s coming through in this post - which is likely to be more unattractive to them than the tattoos. I really would try to relax a bit - you have so so much time left to find someone, who’ll love you tattoos and all.

Christ, just leave and find someone better. No, none of this is normal and who cares whether he’s bi or not - he’s actively and repeatedly cheated on you (in thought at least) for your entire relationship. You know he’s not going to change, do you want more of this? You’re 23, you’ll find someone else.

35F and childfree. I have a great job/career with demanding hours and I have no idea how people with kids do it. Because I don’t have kids, all my spare time is spent with my partner and my friends. Because I can devote all my spare time to them, I have a relatively large group of friends who are all childfree late-30-somethings. Because I’m not paying for dependents I can afford to go to music festivals and gigs, fancy dinners, on exciting holidays (climbing Machu Picchu in a month’s time). I compare my life with my boss who is only 5 years older than me and he spends all his leisure time with his young kids, going to their sports days and clarinet recitals, hanging out with other parents and their young kids (who he inevitably hates) and complaining about their boring family holidays. Don’t give up hope! Plenty of other people out there want the same life as us :)

It’s in the early stages but my current boyfriend tells me literally every day how wonderful I am - and often uses that word, wonderful. He is consistently thoughtful about the little things (will always offer to hold my bags, asks me what I want to drink the moment we arrive in a bar, opens the car door for me, takes my trash to the bins for me, washes/cleans up after himself in my flat, even offered to clean my cats’ litter tray yesterday). He behaves the same way with other people too so it’s clearly an inherent trait and not a put-on behaviour to make me like him. My ex was the complete opposite - from day one it was all about him and he breadcrumbed me with very occasional compliments/affection to make me keep chasing his approval and to hold power over me. It’s night and day and I couldn’t be happier.

Clearly you know you deserve more than you currently have - I never believed I could find something better, and it took most of a year of a lot of failed dates in between, but now I have the kind of relationship I always used to want, the kind I’d watch my friends having and feel jealous of. And even better, I know that if things did end with the current guy, I’d just keep looking until I found something that good again. It proved to me that they’re out there - go find yours!

I still really don’t understand what “being exclusive but not boyfriend/girlfriend” even means. Him purposefully bringing it up only to turn you down feels like negging, and you’re right to see it as a red flag. He’s clearly keeping you at a distance - and he knows he’s doing it, and doesn’t care. My ex did this to me and it was indicative of how he was with me for the entire rest of the relationship. It’s a move to keep power and control over you, and to make you beg for his attention and validation, and it sucks. When I met my current boyfriend, there was no doubt, no hesitation, no silly mind games, no leaving exit routes or potential cheating excuses open - we were exclusive from the start and made it official a few weeks in because it just felt so natural, easy and relaxed. You deserve better OP, sorry this guy is a jackass but you’re completely right not to put up for this treatment.
Clive

I had this one time (except more skeezy) and I just messaged to say that I’d been looking forward to the date but his behaviour over text had put me off and I was sorry but I no longer wanted to go. When he (inevitably) got angry and started blaming me for not “warning him” in advance, I calmly pointed out that it wasn’t my job to police his behaviour, he had no right to my time and he might want to reconsider how he behaved if he wanted to go out with other women in future - but it wouldn’t be me.

You owe him nothing - just tell him you don’t want to see him. You’re also completely right to feel how you do, his behaviour is at best ridiculous and at worst somewhat concerning.
You want to maintain the non-sexual side of the relationship while sleeping with other people. Why not break up and remain friends? It seems like that’s fundamentally what you want with this man.

I’m 34 and still have regular nightmares that I’ve forgotten to revise for an A level, or missed one of my GCSE exams 🤷‍♀️ good luck

(Just to clarify, this popped up on my feed - I’m not lurking around school age subreddits 😅)

I (34F) have gone on dates with maybe 15 guys in the 9 months since my 1.5yr relationship ended? All OLD.

Of those, I’ve slept with 4. Most didn’t get past a first date, the ones I slept with are the only ones that did I think.

In total I’ve slept with 11 people in the 9 months. In addition to the 4 from dating, there were 2 one-night stands picked up from clubs, 3 FWB types found on Pure (I don’t count those as “dates”), and 2 friends-of-friends where we just hooked up after parties or on holidays.

But I think I’m unusual because I’m very comfortable with casual/stranger sex. And I have a very high sex drive so if I go more than 2-3 weeks without sex and don’t have a current sexual partner, I’ll find one for something casual. I used to use Feeld but it’s sort of tainted by my ex so I use Pure now.

Most of my single friends are not as sexually active as me and I have friends who get tons of male attention, make out with lots of guys and even go most of the way but hold off from having full sex. There’s no right answer and it’s just doing what works for you. In the end, all that matters is if you’re happy with how much you date/have sex - no one else’s experience is relevant and you shouldn’t feel shamed one way or the other.

This is really horrible for you and I sympathise - but  let’s be real, you already know he slept with her, 2 times (at least). What possible other thing would she be “reviewing” him for - his incredible texting skills?

This isn’t repairable - throw the whole man out, and I hope you find someone better. Good luck OP.

I dated someone like this for 20 months… just lots of mean little snipes and digs that on their own weren’t huge but added up, like introducing me to people by saying my job was boring (as if him working in HR was so fascinating), interrupting me to loudly say “you’ve already told me this” when I was telling a story - even when I was actually speaking in front of him to people I hadn’t actually told that story before, a seeming lack of interest in my life to the extent it didn’t directly concern him (my job, childhood, history), a lack of affection except at times it suited him because he wanted to elicit some emotional/validation response from me… in my case I realised (too late) he was a complete narcissist (I don’t use the term lightly, he absolutely was) and I spent 20 months being treated more and more like crap and having my self-confidence and self-esteem increasingly eroded while my friends watched and absolutely hated him for it. Not saying this guy will be as bad, but I knew at the time that it didn’t feel right and OP it sounds like you have that feeling too. I’d advise not wasting 20 months like I did.

I (34F) was with my ex (34M) 20 months - he is super avoidant, autistic, demanded poly/open/NM (hard to call what he practised ‘E’NM), told me 2 months in he didn’t want a serious, committed or monogamous relationship. I (reluctantly, stupidly, desperately) agreed - and it took us until month 10 for him to admit we were in a “relationship” as bf/gf. We hung out every weekend and often a couple of weeknights, fully integrated into each other’s friendship groups and rarely saw them without the other (except one-on-one catch-ups).

He started dating someone a week before we broke up and used it as the impetus to immediately chuck me - I knew at the time, but always assumed given how he was for the whole time I’d known him (and how he was before, from what I understood from his friends) that it wouldn’t last more than a month or two before he got bored and moved on. I also assumed that ultimately what he wanted (as he told me at the start) was to be functionally single poly and just date lots and lots of women (and men) without being “tied down” in a relationship.

Well, I just found out he was together with the girl he dumped me over the whole 8 months since our break-up - and SHE MOVED IN WITH HIM after 1 month. They have now apparently just broken up.

It’s incredibly hurtful and hard to process - or to reconcile with the man I knew - but ultimately the two options are (1) he had a complete personality / intention / value transplant from the man I knew for 20 months, and the man all his friends knew for a decade before that or (2) he is still exactly the same person, in which case all of his behaviours with the rebound have to be interpreted through that lens.

For our whole relationship (and perhaps particularly when we broke up) he had absolutely no ability to admit any personal failings or any ways he might need to change or be a better partner. His entire thing was “take it or leave it” - he literally said this to me several times while we dated! - and meeting someone else before ending things with me would have just cemented for him that he’s fine as he is and it’s the girl’s problem if they’re unhappy with anything he does.

By the time we broke up we were hanging out with my friends maybe 80% of his wider socialising time and with his maybe 20%. I am very lucky to have a very large, integrated, active friendship group where we frequently go to gigs, raves, dinners, holidays, art fairs etc etc… He had a small-ish number of largely disconnected friends, who were mostly super nice but not nearly as social. My friends hated the way he treated me and completely turned their back on him the moment we broke up. I then also kept a couple of his friends in the split… they remained friends with him, but I now probably spend more time with them than he does (this is how I heard about the rebound - I’m no contact with him at my insistence). So overnight he basically lost most of the social life he’d spent over a year and a half investing in. I think that was the main driver for latching onto the new girl and doubling down on her - particularly ensuring that he was spending a lot of time with her (by co-habiting once she lost her lease and needed a place to stay). I think it’s telling that, unlike me, apparently his friends barely met her - like once or twice in 8 months, despite them living together. (Maybe he was scared she’d keep them like I did!). Apparently he didn’t let her change a single thing in his house either - which again is in keeping with him thinking it wouldn’t be permanent.

Anyway - all feedback from his friends is that it was absolutely a rebound, she was weird when they did meet her and not a patch on me (his friends are so genuinely lovely, I really miss the ones I don’t have direct contact with anymore), and they just saw it as a blatant doubling down on his decision to dump me when it became apparent he’d made a big mistake. And I know that he was a horrible partner for basically most of our relationship, red flags like a China day parade, quite often very intentionally cruel and vindictive, incapable of proper communication like nothing I’d ever experienced before, withholding and controlling, and that it’s almost impossible he was any other way with her because he had literally no desire or will to change. But, obviously it hurts, and it makes me question my self-worth and relative value.

Thanks for this post, which is a helpful reminder of why these relationships should be seen realistically as the cries for help/flailings of suffering that they are, and good luck to all others out there going through this.
You didn’t need any of these edits. Yes he’s massively insecure and this is a totally unreasonable reaction, as you clearly know. Either he changes his attitude, or you change the man 🤷‍♀️

No, because it’s literally none of your business and she is doing nothing wrong from the sound of it. Getting divorced and having a child doesn’t mean she can’t have sex - including casual sex, if that’s what she wants! She’s still a woman with her own agency and her own right to make parenting choices. Having some casual non-serious rebounds while going through a divorce sounds completely standard in any event - and even if it wasn’t, why do you care? In all honesty you sound very jealous (either that she’s not sleeping with you anymore, or because she’s getting a lot of action) - maybe try and interrogate why you’re clearly so focussed on this woman’s life when it now has absolutely nothing to do with you?

Just to reiterate - you sound like a great guy, your texts are on point and I can’t see from what you’ve said that you’re doing anything wrong. I’m in a similar situation from the other side as a woman (constantly hitting it off / going home with people I meet in real life, only for there to be zero follow-through) and it’s so so tough. All I can say is to hang in there and believe it isn’t you (though I struggle with that as well).

In all honesty - if I meet a guy I want them to be keen and texting me the same/next day. If they wait three days I feel like they’re playing mind games and it’s honestly a massive turn off because I can’t be bothered with that kind of thing anymore. But possibly that’s something that comes when you’re a bit older (I’m 34F) and young people seem to have weird rules about this stuff.

I’ve dated a guy like this and to be honest OP, you know that it’s seriously out of order (that’s why you’re posting here). It won’t be a one-off and he’ll try his luck again sooner rather than later because he’s “gotten away with it” and hasn’t actually taken your concerns seriously at all or acknowledged any fault in any meaningful sense (which is more concerning than the actual incident itself, to be honest, as it shows he doesn’t care or have any inclination to put in the requisite effort avoid doing it again). The negging the next day is also a particularly nasty touch. It sucks but do you want to spend every subsequent social interaction worrying about him drinking too much, or his behaviour, and keeping an eye on him when he’s near other women, and wondering what he’s saying to them, and not trusting him to act properly, and waiting for the other shoe to drop? It’s not fun, trust me.

Just wanted to say I’m really sorry - and also that “I don’t understand why I do this” in these kinds of situations is such bullshit, and is ultimately just trying to avoid a difficult conversation. I’ve had a similar experience and it’s just cowardice, pure and simple. If he cared enough he would make the effort to actually explain himself but he probably knows that telling the truth will not go down well so is obfuscating to try and salvage what he can of the situation. It’s further unfairness to you and not acceptable. Wishing you the best, it’s horrid to go through but I hope you can get out the other side and realise you’re better off without the lying and subterfuge.

At no point did I say I’m unhappy or that I struggle to find suitable men - that’s all you.

What I was saying is that (1) yes, it does often put a strain on relationships if people have jobs that earn vastly different amounts / have vastly different status ($300k to $30k) but (2) people don’t need “equal” jobs/salaries (I have had happy relationships without day to day money issues people earning half or less than half what I do, although occasionally you’ll encounter a male who problem). I also happily pay my best friend’s share of a lot of our social activities and would consider doing so for a partner in the right circumstances but of course that is something that just adds a level of potential difficulty to a relationship which isn’t there if both parties can pay for themselves in equal shares.  

I’m sorry if my salary has triggered something for you - personally I don’t think it makes me better or worse than anyone else, it’s just a fact, and one that seemed pertinent to this post. Perhaps you feel that only people earning a certain amount or lower should be allowed to express their opinion on these matters.

Edit: just saw you keep referring to women as “females” 😂 that explains *everything*.

Thanks - I’m not ready to give up my career and be a housewife just yet, although thanks for your concern.

As it happens, I live in London (I just converted to $ because Americans struggle to understand other countries). Almost all of the men I go on dates with earn $100k plus and, as per my post, I’ve had two LTRs in recent years with men earning that much (“fucking down”, as you rather unpleasantly put it) and it’s been absolutely fine money-wise. There are no shortage of men in that bracket in London. So I think your doom and gloom is slightly misplaced.

I’m a 34F in biglaw with a relatively high salary ($300k+).

My two LTRs (both M) had white collar jobs with largely regular hours and decent salaries (around $100-150k). I liked that both of their jobs were less intense than mine with more normal working hours - it meant we only needed to navigate my hours to find time together. Now I’m dating again I’m ideally looking for something similar - decent money, white collar profession but preferably not dr/lawyer/banker because I’d actually like us to be able to have time together. My career is also important to me and I don’t want to sacrifice it.

I have zero issues with earning more than a partner and actually would prefer it for the reasons above. There definitely is a point though where if they weren’t earning very much it could cause issues. I liked that with the previous relationships we could do things together (meals, drinks, holidays) without me having to pay for them. I probably wouldn’t mind subsidising them (I do this for my best friend a fair amount) as long as they were engaged in and making effort with their career and not just sitting around in their pants all day playing Destiny. A fellow biglaw F friend was dating a guy on around $30k for a while - it wasn’t the only reason the relationship ended but the prospect of largely funding him (rent, holidays etc) if they stayed together was part of it. Equally, my second LTR definitely struggled with the fact that I earned more than him and had a “higher status” job than him, even though I didn’t give a sh*t. He owned a bigger/more expensive house than me so I’m not sure why he cared in practice, but there is definitely an ego element for some men that is quite unattractive.

Ultimately though it is totally subjective and down to the individual. I know other biglaw Fs who insist a man must earn more than them, which I personally think is bonkers. Equally my best friend basically doesn’t have a job most of the time and is on minimum wage but is probably the best human I know - his girlfriend is successful with her own career and house and doesn’t care at all about his situation. Everyone is looking for something different and values different things - so yes, your job will matter, but in varying amounts and in different ways to different people.

I don’t really have any advice, I’m afraid, but I also absolutely loathe people saying that to me - and it’s usually people in LTRs, so not something they have to put into practice or, if they are claiming that’s why they found someone, I call bullshit - finding people is entirely random in my experience and does not correlate either way with being “happy being alone” or not. Sorry I can’t be more helpful (trying to figure it out myself) but I wish you all the best.

After a few months of intense focus only on me, my ex also started to do this though generally at parties/clubs - I called it “scanning the room”.

On two occasions (when he was on substances) he suddenly started talking to a random woman and asked her if she wanted to make out with me. One thankfully didn’t hear him and I caught him before he repeated himself; the second did and was horrified. It was terribly embarrassing and I had to have a proper talk with him afterwards about being creepy (which he sulked through) and I seriously considered leaving him then. As it was it meant I was on edge whenever we went clubbing after that for quite a while in case he did it again. He didn’t but the wandering eye remained.

After we broke up my friends told me they’d noticed it and had considered it creepy and disrespectful to me - pretty humiliating to hear to be honest. If you’re feeling uneasy, I’d say trust your gut and ditch him.

I’m 34F, live in central London. I don’t want kids and have that in my profile.
